content.headline: Building from the edge can be an advantage.
content.lead: I am a Faroese software engineer and entrepreneur. My work sits where technology, learning, business and institution-building meet.
body: I have spent my career turning difficult systems into things people can understand and use: simulation-based learning, data-rich web applications, software companies and, now, a durable memory layer for human and AI collaboration.

Today I lead Usable, chair the board of the University of the Faroe Islands and Ocean Rainforest, and continue selected work through Tøkni. The common thread is capacity: helping people, organisations and small communities act with more knowledge and a longer horizon.
This site is where I write in my own voice about what we are learning along the way.
principles: Context compounds when it is kept alive.
Small places can build globally useful things.
Technology matters most when it strengthens human judgement.
Institutions deserve the same care as products.

content.title: Why I am writing here
content.summary: A personal site should be more than a list of roles. This is a place to keep the thinking that happens between the projects.
content.bodyMarkdown:
A list of titles can tell you where someone spends time. It rarely tells you what they are noticing.

I wanted a place for the second part: the ideas that appear while building companies, working with new technology and helping institutions make decisions with consequences beyond the next quarter.

## The work between the work

Most useful lessons do not arrive as polished announcements. They emerge as a changed assumption, a failed experiment, a surprising conversation or a tool that quietly alters how a team thinks. LinkedIn is good for starting a conversation. Product sites are good for explaining a product. Neither is quite the right permanent home for those field notes.

This site is. I will write about durable AI memory, founder work, learning systems, the Faroe Islands, and the practical business of building from a small place with a wide horizon.

## Why Usable CMS

The site also has to practise what I am working on. Its content lives in Usable, where drafts, published versions and the context behind them can remain connected. The public website is still a fast, independent renderer, with a checked-in fallback if the content service is unavailable.

That split matters. Tools should increase your agency without taking your work hostage.

## A working notebook in public

I expect the writing here to be concrete, occasionally unfinished and revised when reality provides a better answer. The promise is not a stream of certainty. It is a useful record of the work and what it teaches.
